moat_against: No switching costs and no pricing power against Walmart; Dollar General and Five Below contest the same value customer
Import-heavy assortment — tariff costs and refunds have swung reported results in both directions within a year
Core low-income customer squeezed by cumulative food/fuel inflation; traffic growth is thin and ticket-led
Thin operating margins leave little buffer for shrink, wage or freight shocks
moat_for: Store density and proximity across roughly nine and a half thousand stores — the closest, fastest trip for fill-in consumables
Purchasing scale across the fleet and a low-cost small-box operating model
Multi-price format broadens the ticket and is drawing higher-income shoppers, reducing dependence on the most squeezed cohort
Demonstrated pricing flexibility — the base price point was reset and higher price tiers added without breaking traffic
moat_justification: Store density, purchasing scale and a proven ability to move the price architecture (the $1.25 reset, then multi-price) are real, but there are no switching costs, Walmart and Dollar General contest the same basket with deeper pockets, the mix is import- and tariff-exposed, and the core customer is financially squeezed.
name: Dollar Tree, Inc.
one_liner: Narrow-moat discounter (5/10) genuinely improving after the Family Dollar exit, but at $123.73 the price capitalizes a tariff-refund-flattered TTM run-rate — weighted IRR 6.8%, IV@15 $42.05 on the normalized base; clears 15% only below ~$42, and below ~$92 even on the TTM base.
